name: Karl Marx
role: German philosopher, economist and revolutionary socialist (1818-1883)
summary: A German philosopher, economist and journalist who held that history is driven by class struggle rooted in how society produces goods, and that capitalism rests on the exploitation of wage labour. He argued for the revolutionary overthrow of bourgeois rule, a transitional dictatorship of the proletariat, and common ownership of the means of production, leading eventually to a classless society, and he thought peaceful routes were possible in a few countries such as Britain and the United States.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Gotha critique lists health services among the common needs met from the social product before individual distribution in the first phase of communist society, and says that share grows as the new society develops.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The 1880 programme demands a legal minimum wage fixed each year according to local food prices by a workers' statistical commission.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Contrasts the blind rule of supply and demand, the political economy of the middle class, with social production controlled by social foresight, and sides with the latter; Capital looks to production consciously regulated by freely associated men according to a settled plan.

public-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto lists centralisation of credit, transport and communication in the hands of the State and extension of state-owned factories and instruments of production.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Manifesto's transitional measures include a heavy progressive or graduated income tax. The Gotha critique treats an income tax as a bourgeois demand but does not withdraw the Manifesto measure.

unions-good.rationale: Describes workers' organisation into a class that wrests legislative recognition (Ten Hours Bill) and presents trade unions as workers' attempt to organise co-operation between employed and unemployed against capital's laws, which capital denounces.

property-fundamental.rationale: The theory of the Communists can be summed up as abolition of private property; bourgeois property exists for the few only through its non-existence for nine-tenths of the population.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Capital argues that the generalisation of the Factory Acts is necessary and recounts the Ten Hours Act as a victory of the working class's political economy; the Commune banned fines and night-work in bakeries. His aim was to abolish capital, not to regulate it.

cut-welfare.rationale: The 1880 programme makes society responsible for the old and the disabled, and the 1848 Demands have the state provide for those unable to work.

worker-ownership.rationale: Says the Commune aimed to turn means of production into instruments of free and associated labour and praises co-operative factories run without a class of masters; wants co-operative societies to regulate national production on a common plan.

state-harmful.rationale: Mixed: existing states are class instruments and the Commune broke the state machine, and in a classless society the public power loses its political character; but he required a revolutionary proletarian state for the transition.

limit-guns.rationale: Wants the whole proletariat armed with muskets, rifles, cannon and ammunition and never to surrender its arms, and the 1848 Demands call for universal arming of the people.

empower-police-military.rationale: Praises the Commune for abolishing the standing army and stripping the police of political attributes, and for cheap government by removing standing army and state functionarism.

decide-locally.rationale: Mixed: the Communal Constitution gave municipal liberty and delegate assemblies, but he insisted national unity was to be organised, not broken into a federation of small states.

traditional-family.rationale: Argues the bourgeois family rests on capital and private gain and will vanish with capital; Capital calls the Teutonic-Christian family no more final than Roman or Eastern forms and expects a higher family form.

more-religion-public.rationale: Wants the workers' party to liberate conscience from the witchery of religion, praises the Commune's disestablishment of churches, and sees banishing religion from public law as the political method of emancipation.

gradual-change.rationale: Split: communist ends are reached only by the forcible overthrow of existing conditions, yet once in power the proletariat is to wrest capital from the bourgeoisie by degrees through measures that outstrip themselves.

reviewHistory.rationale: The Manifesto says communist ends can be attained only by forcible overthrow of all existing social conditions, and the Commune text rejects taking over the old state.

reviewHistory.rationale: Split: communist ends are reached only by the forcible overthrow of existing conditions, yet once in power the proletariat is to wrest capital from the bourgeoisie by degrees through measures that outstrip themselves.

free-trade.rationale: Argues free trade means freedom of capital, deepens the workers' misery and creates no universal brotherhood; he votes for it only because it hastens social revolution.

nation-first.rationale: Proclaims that the working men have no country and that united action of leading civilised countries is a first condition of emancipation; the International's principle is solidarity.

limit-growth.rationale: The Manifesto wants to increase the total of productive forces as rapidly as possible; Capital also says capitalist production saps the soil and the labourer, but he never proposes limiting growth.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Mixed: praises the productive forces the bourgeoisie created, and calls machinery the most powerful instrument for shortening labour-time, yet shows capital turning it against workers; social change is required.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Preface describes an era of social revolution when productive forces outgrow relations; the Manifesto and Amsterdam speech call for revolution, and force on the Continent.

central-planning.rationale: Wants all instruments of production centralised in the hands of the State, soil improved by a common plan, and co-operative societies regulating national production on a common plan to end capitalist anarchy.

socialized-markets.rationale: In a co-operative society based on common ownership of the means of production, producers do not exchange their products; the Manifesto also speaks of abolition of buying and selling.

land-value-tax.rationale: Accepts the state's appropriation of ground rent as one transitional measure among many, but ridicules Henry George and others for presenting a single tax on rent as the cure for capitalism while leaving wage labour in place.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The Manifesto lists abolition of all rights of inheritance as a transitional measure, and the 1869 report he wrote calls for extending inheritance duties and limiting testamentary inheritance, with the proceeds used for social emancipation.

reviewHistory.rationale: The Manifesto lists abolition of all rights of inheritance as a measure for the transition. No later statement was read in this audit, so medium.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: The Manifesto lists abolition of all rights of inheritance as a transitional measure, and the 1869 report he wrote calls for extending inheritance duties and limiting testamentary inheritance, with the proceeds used for social emancipation.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Says the protective system of his day is conservative while free trade is destructive and hastens revolution; protective duties serve a rising bourgeoisie against feudalism, which is not support for workers.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Calls for centralisation of credit in a state bank with monopoly, state extension of factories and instruments of production, and development of soil by a common plan.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Says petty artisan and small peasant property is being destroyed by industry and needs no abolition, but his programme is common ownership of the means of production, not their dispersal among small owners; Capital expects capitalist private property to be superseded by socialised property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wage-labour is to disappear when capital does; hired labour is a transitory and inferior form destined to disappear before associated labour; in a common-ownership society producers do not exchange products.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Manifesto calls for centralisation of credit in a state national bank with exclusive monopoly, the opposite of leaving money to the market.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Calls monarchy, in Europe at least, the normal incumbrance and indispensable cloak of class rule, and praises the Commune for presupposing its non-existence.

democracy-best.rationale: Favours the democratic republic (the Manifesto wants the proletariat to win the battle of democracy; the Commune supplied really democratic institutions) and calls it the last state form in which the class struggle is fought out. He does not address voters choosing badly.

workers-councils.rationale: Describes the Commune, mostly working men, as a working, not a parliamentary body, executive and legislative at once. These were municipal councils elected by wards, not workplace councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: On Ireland he backed making it independent of England as the sole means of hastening revolution in England (having first thought of a free federation); this is the only case examined.

natural-rulers.rationale: Puts 'natural superiors' in scare quotes when describing how the Commune's working men took public functions from the ruling class, and says public functions ceased to be private property of the government's tools.

political-violence-never.rationale: Says communist ends can be attained only by forcible overthrow, and in the Amsterdam speech says that in most Continental countries the lever of revolution must be force.

separate-church-state.rationale: Treats banishing religion from public law to private law as political emancipation, a big step forward, and praises the Commune's disestablishment and disendowment of all churches.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Criticises the Christian state as the negation of the state and treats religion as an illusion; wants government and church excluded from schools.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Manifesto opens by saying the history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Mixed: the Gotha critique calls equal right a bourgeois defect because equal standards applied to unequal individuals give unequal results, and wants distribution by need; abolishing classes is his aim, but he does not propose equal outcomes as such.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Describes the egoism of civil society and money as alienation and wants the abolition of huckstering; he does not defend self-interest as a moral good.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Mixed but leaning against: praises the productive forces and railways, while Capital says capital saps the soil and the labourer and condemns the human cost of industry.

restore-past-order.rationale: Condemns reactionary socialism and says the bourgeoisie constantly revolutionises production; the movement is forward-looking.

direct-action.rationale: Calls abstention from political action dangerous and fatal for the cause and holds that workers must seize political power, though he also sees force as the lever in most of the Continent.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Gotha critique: the higher phase of communism comes when the enslaving subordination to the division of labour has vanished; Capital wants the detail-worker replaced by the fully developed individual fit for a variety of labours.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Gotha critique: in a higher phase of communist society society inscribes on its banners from each according to ability, to each according to needs.

production-for-use.rationale: Production should be consciously regulated by freely associated men according to a settled plan, and in Communist society accumulated labour is a means to enrich the labourer's existence; capital's aim is surplus value.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Wage-labour creates capital, a property that exploits wage-labour; property rests on antagonism of capital and wage-labour. Capital develops surplus-value from unpaid labour.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Gotha critique says between capitalist and communist society lies a political transition in which the state can be nothing but the revolutionary dictatorship of the proletariat.

collective-farming.rationale: The Manifesto calls for industrial armies for agriculture and common-plan cultivation, and Capital expects land and other means of production to become socialised and common.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Counts colonial systems, public debts, protection and commercial wars among the products of capital's early growth, and notes looting overseas flowed back and became capital; he did not state a general law of imperialist war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Proposes a heavy progressive income tax and public use of land rents, and treats taxes as the economic basis of the government machinery; he does not regard taxation as theft.

conscription.rationale: Proposes general armament and military instruction of the people, with every male citizen serving for a very limited time in small standing armies as a transitional necessity.

positive-liberty.rationale: Says bourgeois freedom means only free buying and selling and wants an association in which the free development of each is the condition for the free development of all.

total-state.rationale: Calls state education objectionable, wants government and church excluded from schools, and wants the state made completely subordinate to society.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Condemns foreign policy of piratical wars and Russian encroachments, though he saw British conquest of India as an unconscious historical tool.

bound-labor.rationale: Calls serfdom and slave-labour barbaric horrors and says the bourgeoisie tore asunder feudal ties.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Mixed: the Manifesto says the ruling ideas of each age are those of its ruling class and jurisprudence is the will of a class, yet he treats his own analysis as scientific.

universal-morality.rationale: Rejects the claim that Freedom and Justice are eternal truths common to all states of society; says such ideas are outgrowths of bourgeois conditions.

single-common-good.rationale: Treats politics as class struggle in which ruling-class notions are presented as laws for all; the proletariat is to overthrow the other classes rather than balance or reconcile.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Praises co-operative factories that run without a class of masters employing hands, and the Commune's handing of closed workshops to associations of workmen.

national-self-determination.rationale: Supports Polish national emancipation and Irish independence, calling it a condition of workers' emancipation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Criticism of religion disillusions people so they think and act like men who have regained their senses; truth is to be proved in practice.

class-collaboration.rationale: Criticises schemes that deaden the class struggle and reconcile class antagonisms; the workers' movement is class struggle.

workers-nation.rationale: Says the working men have no country and ends with Working Men of All Countries, Unite; the International's principle is solidarity.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Describes the state power as the national power of capital over labour, a public force organised for social enslavement, an engine of class despotism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Describes the bourgeois husband treating his wife as a mere instrument of production and bourgeois marriage as a system of wives in common.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Describes governments of the ruling classes as hotbeds of debt, place, pelf and patronage and the Second Empire's elite as plunderers.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Wants the state to centralise credit, communication, transport and production.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1880 preamble he dictated says the emancipation of the producing class is that of all human beings without distinction of sex or race, and the programme seeks to remove the legal articles making workers inferior to employers and women to men.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Says united action of the leading civilised countries is one of the first conditions for emancipation, and that the Commune fell because other centres developed no comparable movement.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Says government and church should be equally excluded from any influence on the school, and praises the Commune for opening education free of church and state interference.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Attributes historical change to class struggle and the development of productive forces; competition among workers is what continually upsets their organisation.

separated-powers.rationale: Praises the Commune as a working body, executive and legislative at once, and judges elective and revocable; no checks between separate bodies are described.

vanguard-party.rationale: Mixed: the Manifesto calls the Communists the most advanced and resolute section pushing others forward who understand the line of march, but says they form no separate sectarian party, and the Gotha critique stresses workers' own class movement.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Says the pretended natural law of population reduces to the law of capitalist accumulation and that relative surplus population is produced by capital.

party-controls-media.rationale: The 1880 programme demands the abolition of all laws over the press, meetings and associations; in 1842 he called the abolition of censorship its only real, radical cure.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Praises the Commune because from its members downward the public service was done at workman's wage and representation allowances disappeared.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Attacks the Prussian censorship, including its aim of suppressing what offends morality, and says the radical cure for censorship is its abolition.

recall-officials.rationale: The Commune's councillors were responsible and revocable at short terms, and all officials, including magistrates and judges, elective, responsible and revocable; he approves.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Commune's first decree was the suppression of the standing army and its replacement by the armed people; rural areas were to have a national militia.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Says the bourgeoisie rescued a considerable part of the population from the idiocy of rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Calls for restoring partitioned Poland on a democratic basis, and says it is the German workers' special duty because Germany is one of the partitioners.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Contested: describes India as stagnant Asiatic society needing regeneration and speaks of superior and inferior civilisations, but he also exposes bourgeois civilisation's hypocrisy and barbarism.

death-penalty.rationale: Says it would be very difficult if not impossible to found the justice or expediency of capital punishment on any principle, and condemns a society that knows no better defence than the hangman.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Says political emancipation is not human emancipation and that the Irish land question is inseparable from the national question.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Praises the Commune's disestablishment and disendowment of churches as proprietary bodies and the priests' return to private life.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Rejects the London press's case for letting the South secede and backs the Union's war against the slaveholders' secession.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Every programme he drafted asks for graduated taxation: a heavy progressive income tax (Manifesto), strongly progressive taxes (1848), and a progressive tax on incomes over 3,000 francs (1880).

character-from-environment.rationale: Says consciousness changes with material conditions and, in Theses on Feuerbach, that the human essence is the ensemble of social relations, though circumstances are changed by men.

land-redistribution.rationale: Wants large estates taken, but in 1850 tells workers to oppose giving feudal lands to the peasants and to keep them as state property farmed collectively, and in 1872 says giving the soil to associated rural labourers would surrender society to one class.

reviewHistory.rationale: Backs agrarian revolution in Ireland and in Poland and the abolition of landed property, but his own programme directs land rents to public purposes rather than to individual farmers.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Wants large estates taken, but in 1850 tells workers to oppose giving feudal lands to the peasants and to keep them as state property farmed collectively, and in 1872 says giving the soil to associated rural labourers would surrender society to one class.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The 1859 Preface says the mode of production of material life conditions social, political and intellectual life, and that social existence determines consciousness.

ban-cartels.rationale: Treats centralisation of capital as a historical advance that socialises labour, and ridicules petty-bourgeois attempts to restore old forms; the remedy is expropriation, not breaking up concentrations.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Praises the world market and the end of old local and national seclusion; he does not advocate autarkic blocs.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Holds that no social order is destroyed before its productive forces have developed, and calls the proletarian movement the self-conscious movement of the immense majority.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Treats the revolution that swept away estates, guilds and privileges as a big step forward within the old order, and calls monarchy a cloak of class rule.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mixed: England was an unconscious tool of history bringing a regenerating revolution to India, but its crimes are denounced and he expects Indians to throw off the English yoke.

public-money-creation.rationale: Calls for centralisation of credit in the hands of the state through a national bank with state capital and monopoly.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Expects commercial crises to return and each time threaten society, and that the monopoly of capital becomes a fetter and the capitalist integument is burst asunder.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Describes the English working class as exploited and impoverished by capital; says Irish workers' antagonism with English ones is kept alive by the ruling classes. He did not say workers in rich countries were not exploited.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rejects monarchy and praises the Commune's elected, revocable officials in place of hereditary rule.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Ridicules philanthropists, humanitarians and charity organisers as bourgeois socialism that wants capitalism without its dangers.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Says workers who abstain from political action would lose Heaven on Earth like the old Christians who despised politics.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Says the ruling ideas of each age are the ruling class's, yet also describes the state as a public force organised for enslavement, so both consent and force appear.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Describes colonial looting and plunder of India flowing back to become capital in the mother country and English free trade destroying native industry.

native-born-offices.rationale: Praises the Commune for admitting foreigners and making a German working man its Minister of Labour.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Argues that the secession and the war were based throughout on the slave question, a struggle between the system of slavery and the system of free labour.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Reports without criticism that the Commune pulled down the Vendome Column, a symbol of martial glory, to mark a new era.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Describes delegates to the National Delegation as revocable at any time and bound by the mandat imperatif of their constituents, as part of the Commune constitution he endorses.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Wants abolition of property in land with its rents applied to public purposes and land transformed into common means of production; he does not speak of tenure by use.

corporate-influence.rationale: Says lords of land and capital use their political privileges to defend economic monopolies and the House of Commons is a house of landed proprietors; he does not speak of lobbying and campaign money.

job-guarantee.rationale: The 1848 Demands call for national workshops, with the state guaranteeing the livelihood of all workers and providing for those unable to work.

informal-organisation.rationale: Backs organised political action, a workers' party and a centralised International whose General Council had widened powers, and rejects abstentionists.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Manifesto says communists do not abolish personal appropriation of products for the maintenance of life, only the power to subjugate others' labour; Gotha has labour certificates for individual consumption.

defeat-communism.rationale: As a communist he sought world domination by the proletariat and the forcible overthrow of existing conditions.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religion is the illusory happiness of the people and the opium of the people; the religious reflex vanishes when practical relations offer only intelligible relations to men and nature.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The bourgeoisie has played a most revolutionary part and created more massive productive forces than all preceding generations; he also sees it as creating the conditions for socialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Says the real point is to do away with the status of women as mere instruments of production, which follows the abolition of the present system of production.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Criticises utopian socialists' isolated phalansteres, Home Colonies and Little Icaria as castles in the air.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Advocates communism and treats capitalism as a transient stage to be overthrown.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Denounces British rule in India as atrocious extortion, the hypocrisy and barbarism of bourgeois civilisation, and colonial plunder in Capital.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Praises the Commune where plain working men took public affairs into their hands and public functions ceased to be a privilege of the government's tools.

alienated-labor.rationale: Capital describes machinery and the division of labour as turning the worker into a fragment of a man and estranging intellectual potentialities of the labour process; the 1844 manuscripts give the early account.

social-market-economy.rationale: Treats markets and wage-labour as to be superseded, not combined with social protection.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Calls Proudhon's free credit and people's bank, as the basis for transforming society, an out-and-out petty-bourgeois fantasy resting on a misunderstanding of commodities and money, though credit can help workers' emancipation in some conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Supports universal suffrage in the Commune and notes a property qualification keeps non-owners out of politics.

reification.rationale: Describes commodity fetishism: relations between people take the form of relations between things.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Says the concentration of land in few hands deepens landlords' power and that lords of capital use political privileges to block workers' emancipation.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Says everyone should attend to religious needs without police interference and wants the church and the government both kept out of schools; criticises the state as educator.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Ridicules organised charity as bourgeois socialism; the Gotha critique places poor relief inside the social product, but he did not praise state programmes either.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The 1880 programme demands removal of all articles of the Civil Code establishing the inferiority of woman in relation to man.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Says those who work acquire nothing and those who acquire anything do not work in bourgeois society; distribution in the first phase of communism is by labour performed.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Holds that politics is class struggle driven by material conditions, not a spiritual struggle of good and evil.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Wants the proletariat raised to ruling class and the Commune as a government of the working class, with workers holding political power.

municipal-property.rationale: Wants means of production centralised by the State and co-operative societies regulating national production on a common plan, not owned by separate local communities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Says the Communal Constitution has been mistaken for a break-up into a federation of small states and was to organise national unity; delegates were bound but a few central functions remained.

free-public-college.rationale: Says free higher education institutions merely defray the education of the upper classes from general tax receipts; he backs free elementary schooling in the Manifesto.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Praises replacing the standing army by the armed people, but the Commune's armed force was itself a public body.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Says the individual contract between capital and labour can never be struck on equitable terms, and that union action on wages and hours is legitimate and necessary while the present system lasts.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Says the working class cannot simply lay hold of the ready-made state machinery and wield it for its own purposes; the Commune was the destruction of the state power that stood above society.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Mixed: says the working class has no ready-made utopias to introduce, but lays out definite measures and a common national plan.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Rejects an abstract human essence inherent in each individual, calling it the ensemble of the social relations.

workers-own-party.rationale: Says the working class must fight on political as well as social grounds and that workers must seize political power; the Inaugural Address notes the political organisation of the workingmen's party.

indirect-election.rationale: Describes the Commune plan in which rural district assemblies of delegates send deputies to a national delegation, each revocable and bound by instructions, and calls it the Communal Constitution.

national-church-status.rationale: Approves disestablishment and disendowment of all churches.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Calls for the abolition of taxes on consumption (1848), the total abolition of indirect taxes because they raise prices and hide what people pay (1866), and again the abolition of all indirect taxes (1880).

automate-paid-work.rationale: Says machinery considered alone shortens the hours of labour, and that the shortening of the working day is the basic prerequisite of the realm of freedom.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Capital opens with value as congealed human labour.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Says workers have no country but the proletariat must constitute itself the nation, itself national though not in the bourgeois sense.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Tells workers to replace 'a fair day's wage for a fair day's work' with the watchword 'Abolition of the wages system!', and calls hired labour a transitory form destined to give way to associated labour.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Split: the Amsterdam speech allows that workers in America, England and perhaps Holland may win by peaceful means but says force is the lever in most of the Continent; the 1880 preamble uses universal suffrage as one means but says collective ownership can arise only from the proletariat's revolutionary action.

no-central-bank.rationale: Calls for credit centralised in a national bank with state capital and an exclusive monopoly, and in 1848 for all private banks to be replaced by a state bank.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: The 1848 Demands want the state bank's notes to be legal tender, gradually replacing gold and silver with paper money as the means of exchange.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: Demands a heavy progressive income tax for the transition (1848), while the Gotha critique notes that an income tax presupposes the separate class incomes of capitalist society.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: The 1848 Demands appeal to the proletariat, petty bourgeoisie and peasantry to carry them out together, and the Eighteenth Brumaire says the impoverished small farmers find their natural allies and leaders in the urban proletariat.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: Drafted with Guesde a minimum programme of immediate demands (eight-hour day, minimum wage, tax reform) on which the workers' party was to fight elections, and called the legal limitation of the working day a preliminary condition of all further emancipation.

wages-fall-to-bare-minimum.rationale: Rejects Lassalle's iron law of wages as Malthusian dogma, and says the value of labour includes a traditional standard of life beyond mere physical needs, though capitalism tends to push wages down towards their minimum limit.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Says the land can only be owned by the nation itself, not by peasants or rural associations, and the Manifesto's first measure is the abolition of property in land.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: Hails the Ten Hours Act and the co-operative factories as victories of the political economy of labour over the political economy of property.

country-wealth-only-from-land.rationale: Holds that value is congealed human labour, and that labour and nature together are the sources of use values and wealth.

pay-for-effort.rationale: Accepts payment by the amount of labour (its duration or intensity) only in the first phase of communism, calls it a defect of bourgeois right, and wants it replaced by distribution according to need.

state-finances-worker-businesses.rationale: Split: in 1864 he wants co-operative labour developed to national dimensions and fostered by national means, but in 1875 he scorns producers' co-operatives with state aid as a Lassallean substitute for the workers' own revolutionary transformation.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: Accepts free elementary schooling, but says free higher education and free civil justice for all only defray the costs of the upper and possessing classes from general taxes.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: The Manifesto lists equal liability of all to work among the transitional measures, and the 1866 Instructions say that in a rational society no able-bodied adult should be exempt from working in order to eat.

physical-labour-duty.rationale: Says no able-bodied adult ought to be exempted from working in order to eat, and to work not only with the brain but with the hands too.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: Places a political transition period, the revolutionary dictatorship of the proletariat, between capitalist and communist society, and a first phase of communism still marked by the old society before the higher phase.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: Nulled: this id now asks whether social change should respect established institutions (reused 2026-11-10); this answer was to its earlier text, "Social reform should proceed in small steps.", and moved to gradual-change, which now has that text.

reviewHistory.rationale: Split: communist ends are reached only by the forcible overthrow of existing conditions, yet once in power the proletariat is to wrest capital from the bourgeoisie by degrees through measures that outstrip themselves.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled: this id now asks whether social change should respect established institutions (reused 2026-11-10); this answer was to its earlier text, "Social reform should proceed in small steps.", and moved to gradual-change, which now has that text.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: Declares that communist ends can be attained only by forcible overthrow of all existing social conditions, and that in most Continental countries force must be the lever of the revolution.

property-sabotage-justified.rationale: Treats Luddite machine-breaking as an early error: workers had to learn to attack not the material instruments of production but the way capital employs them.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: Says free trade would make relations between nations no more fraternal than between classes, and that calling cosmopolitan exploitation universal brotherhood is a bourgeois idea.

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: Describes the Asiatic, ancient, feudal and bourgeois modes of production as epochs marking progress in the economic development of society.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: Denounces, with heavy irony, the extirpation, enslavement and entombment in mines of the aboriginal population of the Americas as part of the bloody 'rosy dawn' of capitalist production.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: Split: the Gotha critique expects labour in higher communism to become life's prime want, while Capital vol. 3 places the true realm of freedom beyond labour dictated by necessity, with a shorter working day as its basic prerequisite.

technology-never-politically-neutral.rationale: Split: he says many inventions since 1830 were made to arm capital against workers' revolts, but also that machinery in itself shortens and lightens labour, the harm coming from its capitalist employment.

pay-off-national-debt.rationale: The 1880 programme he drafted with Guesde demands the suppression of the public debt, that is, its cancellation rather than repayment.

member-state-blocks-federal-overreach.rationale: Tells workers to oppose a federal republic and broad provincial autonomy that would paralyse the central government, and to seek the most decisive centralisation of power.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: Says the tradition of past generations weighs on the brains of the living, and the social revolution must draw its poetry from the future and let the dead bury their dead.

notes: Mature positions are used. The Manifesto (1848) was co-written with Engels but signed by Marx and counts as his words; the German Ideology is also co-written and unpublished in his lifetime and used only lightly. The 1843-44 texts (On the Jewish Question, Hegel introduction) and 1844 manuscripts are early. Engels' later writings are not treated as Marx's positions. In 1869-70 he moved from a free federation of Ireland and Britain to Irish independence; the 1872 Amsterdam speech allows a peaceful route in Britain, the United States and perhaps Holland. Opus pass (2026-11-10, rules 5): brought the audit up to rules 5 (every source tagged as words: Marx never held office, so there is no record of acts), answered the candidate statements, and searched the local Marxists Internet Archive corpus by theme for works the first pass had not read: the 1848 Demands of the Communist Party in Germany, the March 1850 Address, the 1853 article on capital punishment, the 1861 Civil War articles, Value, Price and Profit, the 1866 Geneva Instructions, the 1869 inheritance report, the 1872 Nationalisation of the Land, the 1880 French Workers' Party programme, Gotha part II, Capital vol. 3 ch. 48, the 1842 censorship texts and the letters on Proudhon (1865) and Henry George (1881). Land redistribution changed from 1 to -1 (he wanted estates kept as state property, not given to farmers), and the inheritance answer rose to high on the 1869 report. Themes searched without a stated position: technology, ecology and climate, gender identity, sexuality, drugs, immigration levels, international bodies and most modern world-order questions, which postdate him or he never addressed; they stay null.
